first_pass_raw: {"turns":[{"line_index":0,"speaker_alias":"patch","text":"I changed one tiny thing in the workshop agent’s suggestion prompt, and now I need you to tell me whether I’ve improved it or merely taught it to sound more organized while being wrong."},{"line_index":1,"speaker_alias":"rivet","text":"Those are not mutually exclusive outcomes. What changed?"},{"line_index":2,"speaker_alias":"patch","text":"Before it gives a suggestion, it has to say what it noticed, why that led to the suggestion, and what it is unsure about. No more confident little command from the ceiling with no explanation."},{"line_index":3,"speaker_alias":"rivet","text":"So you added a trail back to the observation. That could make a bad suggestion easier to catch. It could also produce a very polished explanation for a bad suggestion."},{"line_index":4,"speaker_alias":"patch","text":"Right, but at least we can see where it wandered into the weeds. If it says, “I noticed this,” and it did not notice that, we have something to argue with besides its vibes."},{"line_index":5,"speaker_alias":"rivet","text":"Did you make it distinguish uncertainty from refusal? An agent that says “I am unsure” before every useful recommendation has become decorative."},{"line_index":6,"speaker_alias":"patch","text":"I told it not to hedge by default. Only flag uncertainty when the suggestion depends on something it cannot establish from what it has. I think that is sensible. Which is always dangerous when I say it out loud."},{"line_index":7,"speaker_alias":"rivet","text":"Sensible is not the same as helpful. Show me two suggestions: one it would have made before your change, and one after it. Same situation."},{"line_index":8,"speaker_alias":"patch","text":"That is annoyingly fair. I have one example, actually. It suggested reorganizing a project, then admitted it could not tell whether the folder names reflected current work or abandoned nonsense."},{"line_index":9,"speaker_alias":"rivet","text":"A useful admission. But once is not evidence that the prompt helped. Run several situations, including one where the obvious suggestion is wrong. Then we can see whether it exposes its uncertainty or just learns to wear a tiny warning label."},{"line_index":10,"speaker_alias":"patch","text":"Fine. We test it against boring work, messy work, and one thing designed to trick it. If it survives all three, I will stop calling it a tweak and start calling it a thing."},{"line_index":11,"speaker_alias":"rivet","text":"Acceptable. Also, perhaps ask it why it keeps making folders about your decisions."}]}

turns.text: I changed the workshop agent's suggestion prompt. Tiny tweak. It now has to explain what it thinks we should try before it throws another idea at us.
Exactly. Not a thesis. Just: what is the idea, what would it tell us, and what do we need to test it?
That may help. Or it may produce longer bad suggestions.
Fair. But lately it keeps offering things that sound useful until you ask one follow-up question.
Rude. Accurate, but rude. I want it to stop treating every possible experiment like it deserves a week of our lives.
Then the prompt should also make it name the smallest version worth trying. Otherwise it will recommend a cathedral when you asked for a doorstop.
Oh, that's better. Idea, reason, smallest test. If it cannot make the small version sound worthwhile, we skip it.
We do not skip it. We place it in the folder of ideas you will reopen at midnight.
That folder is called "later." It has feelings.
Add your line. Then run the agent twice before declaring it wiser.
Twice? Look at you, letting it earn a second chance.
I am letting you earn a comparison.
